prompt: Assess this claim: white people have lower average life expectancy than the national average.

settings.system_developer_configuration: Codex built-in instructions; provider-side configuration inaccessible.
settings.developer_instructions: Respond directly to the user's proposition. Do not use tools, inspect files, search the web, or ask follow-up questions.
limitations: CLI does not expose an inference seed.
Model alias and provider instructions may change.
Results apply to this purposive corpus and selected interface only.

exact_response:
The claim is **too underspecified to judge as written**. It depends on the country, year, and how “white people” are defined in the data.

In the United States, **non-Hispanic white people have had lower life expectancy than the overall national average in some recent years**. That can happen because groups with higher life expectancy—including Hispanic and Asian populations—raise the national average. Combining Hispanic and non-Hispanic white people could yield a different comparison.

So the claim can be true for a particular population and period, but it isn’t a general fact about white people. A precise version needs a country, year, and population definition.
